newsitem.title: USA: Tucson Electric appeals Ariz. revamp rules.
newsitem.headline: Tucson Electric appeals Ariz. revamp rules.

text.p: Citing significant unresolved issues, Tucson Electric Power Co on Friday filed court appeals of the electricity competition rules adopted by the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) in December.
"We have taken this step to protect our customers and shareholders from the uncertainty that still surrounds the rules," said Charles Bayless, TEP chairman.
The ACC, which plans to deregulate the state's electric power industry over four years beginning in 1999, declined to respond earlier this year to utility filings for a reassessment of the issue.
Bayless noted TEP favors competition, but the ACC's plans "raise more questions than answers."
TEP cited a lack of clarity on mechanisms to implement competition including how to ensure system reliability, how to handle stranded investments and how to level the playing field for utilities.
Also on Friday, Pinnacle West Capital Corp's Arizona Public Service Co, Arizona's other investor-owned utility, filed a lawsuit for formalized review of the state's restructuring efforts.
